paper.title: Prudent-Banker: No Extra Fees for Baseline Safety in Adversarial Bandits With and Without Delays

settings.name_in_paper: Delayed adversarial bandits with an exploratory safe baseline
unmapped: the learner is given a safe baseline policy x^c in the simplex with x^c(a) >= delta_c for all arms (Assumption 2.1) and also measures regret against x^c
the learner knows the baseline x^c and its minimum mass delta_c
total delay D is unknown to the learner
settings.definition_quote: We consider adversarial bandits with delayed feedback over horizon $T$ against an oblivious adversary. At each round $t\in [T]$, the adversary chooses $\ell_t\in[0,1]^A$ and delay $d_t\in\mathbb N_0$; the learner chooses $x_t\in\Delta_A$, samples $A_t\sim x_t$, incurs unobserved loss $\ell_{t,A_t}$, and observes $(A_t,\ell_{t,A_t})$ at the end of round $t+d_t$. ... There exists a constant $\delta \in (0, 1/A]$ such that $x^c(a) \ge \delta$ for all arms $a \in [A]$.

settings.definition_quote: Consider the batched bandit game with block lengths \(L_1,\dots,L_n\): in block \(m\), the learner chooses actions \(J_{m,1},\dots,J_{m,L_m}\in[A]\) sequentially, but without observing any loss from the current block; after the block ends, the learner observes the chosen losses

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: For any delay sequence with total delay $D$, let $\{x_t\}_{t=1}^T$ be the strategies generated by \textsc{Prudent-Banker} with step-size schedule ... Then \( \mathcal R_T \le \widetilde O\!\left(\sqrt{C_1C_2}(\sqrt T+\sqrt D)\right) \text{ and } \mathcal R_T(x^c) \le O(1+\log D) = \widetilde O(1).\)

results.notes: With negative entropy, C_1 C_2 = log(K)/delta_c, giving O_tilde(delta_c^{-1/2}(sqrt T + sqrt D)). Appendix theorem 'Global Regret and Safety Guarantee' restates this. Proof sums over O(log D) stages, so extra log factors.

results.notes: Comparator regret R(x^c) = E[sum <l_t, x_t - x^c>] against the designated safe baseline (a fixed mixed policy); comparator field set to best_fixed_action for lack of a better value.

source.label: cor:nondelayed-optimal
source.quote: In the non-delayed setting $D=0$, instantiating \textsc{Prudent-Banker} with negative-entropy regularization where $C_1C_2=\log A/\delta$ gives \[ \mathcal R_T \le \widetilde O\!\left(\sqrt{{\delta^{-1}{T\log A}}}\right), \qquad \mathcal R_T(x^c) \le O(1). \]

results.notes: Paper claims this matches Omega(sqrt(T/delta)) lower bound of Muller et al. up to logs.

conditions: regret measured against the safe baseline x^c with x^c(a) >= delta_c

source.label: cor:nondelayed-optimal
source.quote:
In the non-delayed setting $D=0$, instantiating \textsc{Prudent-Banker} with
negative-entropy regularization where $C_1C_2=\log A/\delta$ gives
\[
\mathcal R_T
\le
\widetilde O\!\left(\sqrt{{\delta^{-1}{T\log A}}}\right),
\qquad
\mathcal R_T(x^c)
\le O(1).
\]
Consequently, \textsc{Prudent-Banker} matches the safety-constrained lower
bound of order $\Omega(\sqrt{T/\delta})$ up to logarithmic factors.

results.notes: Comparator regret against the safe baseline x^c.

source.label: thm:delay-side-safety-lb-informal
source.quote: There exist delay sequences with total delay $D$ and a safe comparator $x^c$ satisfying $\min_i x_i^c\ge\delta$ such that every delayed bandit algorithm satisfies, for some adversarial loss sequence, \[ \mathcal R_T(x^c)\le \log D \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathcal R_T \ge \widetilde\Omega\!\left(\delta^{-1/2}\sqrt D\right). \]

results.notes: Informal statement; formal version in appendix. Combined with Muller et al. no-delay bound the paper states Omega(sqrt(T/delta)+sqrt(D/delta)) minus lower-order terms.

symbols.delta_c: minimum probability the safe baseline x^c places on every arm

conditions: algorithms satisfying R_T(x^c) <= log D on the constructed loss sequence
delays d_t >= 1 integer, non-increasing, d_t <= T+1-t

source.label: delayed-safe-lb
source.quote: Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/A]\) and assume \(\delta \ge \frac{L_j}{64V_j}.\) Then there exists a comparator \(x^c\in\Delta_A\) with \(x^c(i)\ge \delta\) such that for every delayed adversarial bandit algorithm there exists an oblivious deterministic delayed-loss sequence ... for which R_T^{del}(x^c;\ell)\le \log D \Rightarrow \max_x R_T^{del}(x;\ell) \ge \frac{3}{256}\delta^{-1/2}\sqrt{V_j/L_j} - ...

results.notes: Second displayed form replaces V_j by D_{bar S_j} (delay outside first j buckets) in the leading term; V_j >= D_{bar S_j}.

symbols.delta_c: minimum probability the safe baseline x^c places on every arm

conditions: algorithms satisfying R_T(x^c) <= log D on the constructed loss sequence
delay sequence d_t = min{q, T+1-t} with T=(N+1)q, q=1

source.label: linear-total-delay
source.quote: Fix integers \(q\ge 1\) and \(N\ge 1\), set \(T:=(N+1)q,\) and define the non-increasing delay sequence \(d_t := \min\{q,T+1-t\}\) ... for which $R_T^{del}(x^c;\ell)\le \log D$ implies \[\max_{x}R_T^{del}(x;\ell) \ge \frac{3}{256}\,\delta^{-1/2}\sqrt{D} - \frac{\sqrt{\log D}}{32\sqrt{2}}\,\delta^{-3/4}D^{1/4} -\log D \text{ for } q =1\]

results.notes: With q=1 delays are all 1 so D=T in this construction.

symbols.delta_c: minimum probability the safe baseline places on every arm

source.label: batched-safe-lb
source.quote: Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/A]\) and \(\Lambda\ge 0\), and assume \(\delta \ge \frac{L_1}{64V}.\) Then there exists a comparator \(x^c\in\Delta_A\) with \(x^c(i)\ge \delta\) such that for every batched bandit algorithm there exists an oblivious deterministic block-loss sequence ... for which R^{bat}(x^c;g)\le \Lambda \Longrightarrow \max_x R^{bat}(x;g) \ge \frac{3}{256}\delta^{-1/2}\sqrt{V/L_1} - ...

results.notes: Intermediate lower bound for batched game used for the delayed reduction.
